findings.F1: The tested effect points the right way but is small against its noise. On folds B and C, the regime's 5-day grid cases number 61. Their mean unusual 5-day move is +0.6 % (t 0.34) and their median is +1.6 %, with 59 % of cases positive. Step 5's own measure over all folds is +2.05 % with t 0.75, on 42 cases across 27 days.
findings.F2: The effect is mixed across periods and coins. Window w17 shows +5.3 % (t 2.04, 11 cases) and window w16 shows −8.2 % (t −1.41, 12 cases). By coin, XMR shows +4.6 % (8 cases) and BTC +2.9 % (9 cases), while LTC shows −1.8 % (12 cases) and ZEC −1.6 % (9 cases).
findings.F3: The rebound appears sooner than the plan's 5 days and fades by day 5. On fresh breaks inside the regime (39 cases, day-clustered), the unusual move is +3.5 % after 1 day (t 1.29), +2.3 % after 2 days (t 1.12), +2.8 % after 3 days (t 1.11) and −1.3 % after 5 days (t −0.26). The regime's grid cases also gain +4.9 % on average over 1 day.
findings.F4: Deeper breaks are followed by larger rises, more clearly over the first day than over five.
findings.F5: Outside the falling, wide-range regime, a monthly low is followed by further falling, so the regime filter carries the effect.
findings.F6: The test is starved of cases, not of size. The book trades only 0.0037 times per coin-day and is in a position on 7 % of coin-days, yet the total move of +2.66 % per case is 13.8 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. More coins would add cases without making the move smaller than the cost.

ideas.idea: In a coin that has fallen over the past 30 days and whose daily high-low ranges over that month are wide compared with its own past year, a close below its lowest low of the prior 30 days is followed by a rise over the next 5 days. The further that close sits below the prior 30-day low, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: Rebound. By the time a volatile decline breaks to a new monthly low, the forced sellers are used up, so buyers and short-covering lift price.

ideas.consequence: A trader would take the rebound right after a deep monthly low in a volatile decline and be out within a day or two, before the bounce fades.
